section: Population policy of India - NPP 2000, family welfare programme, ageing and migration issues
subsections: Family planning programme - launch year, first country, phases of approach
Family welfare schemes - objective and target group
Barriers to family planning - rural factors, sterilisation, couple protection rate
National Population Policy 2000 - objectives, stabilisation target years
Population stabilisation incentives - two-child norms, seat freeze amendments

accepted.s: India became the first country in the world to launch a national family planning programme in which year?
accepted.x: India was the first country to launch a national family planning programme, and it was launched in 1952.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive first-country and launch-year combination.
accepted.sec: Family planning programme - launch year, first country, phases of approach

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the approach to family planning during the 1950s, corresponding to the First and Second Five-Year Plans?
accepted.x: The family planning programme followed a clinic-based approach during the 1950s, particularly during the First and Second Plans.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the successive phases by matching the decade with its approach.
accepted.sec: Family planning programme - launch year, first country, phases of approach

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the phases of India's family planning programme:
1. The 1960s witnessed an extension-education approach along with targets.
2. The programme was renamed the Family Welfare Programme in 1977.
3. The target-free approach was introduced during 1996-97.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 1960s saw extension education and targets, the programme was renamed in 1977, and the target-free approach began in 1996-97.
accepted.tq: Verify the chronological sequence of programme approaches.
accepted.sec: Family planning programme - launch year, first country, phases of approach

accepted.s: The coercive sterilisation drive associated with the Emergency period took place during:
accepted.x: Coercive sterilisation occurred during the 1976-77 Emergency period, following the first National Population Policy of 1976.
accepted.tq: Use the year-pair trap involving the Emergency and sterilisation.
accepted.sec: Family planning programme - launch year, first country, phases of approach

accepted.s:
Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?

1. 1950s — Clinic-based approach
2. 1960s — Extension-education approach with targets
3. 2000 — Voluntary, informed choice and target-free approach
accepted.x: All three combinations are correctly matched with the respective phases of the family planning programme.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure decade-approach pair and check the remaining pairs.
accepted.sec: Family planning programme - launch year, first country, phases of approach

accepted.s: The Reproductive and Child Health approach was associated with the transition from the target-free approach introduced during:
accepted.x: The target-free approach was introduced in 1996-97 and was followed by the Reproductive and Child Health approach.
accepted.tq: Identify the transition year rather than the later policy year.
accepted.sec: Family planning programme - launch year, first country, phases of approach

accepted.s:
Which of the following is the focus of the current family planning approach mentioned in relation to reproductive health?

1. Healthy Timing and Spacing of Pregnancies
2. Nayi Pahel kits
3. Saas Bahu Sammelans
4. FP-LMIS
accepted.x: The current focus includes Healthy Timing and Spacing of Pregnancies, Nayi Pahel kits, Saas Bahu Sammelans and FP-LMIS.
accepted.tq: Test a complete list through the all-inclusive option.
accepted.sec: Family planning programme - launch year, first country, phases of approach

accepted.s: Janani Suraksha Yojana was launched in 2005 under which programme?
accepted.x: Janani Suraksha Yojana was launched in 2005 under the National Rural Health Mission.
accepted.tq: Apply the scheme-parent programme association.
accepted.sec: Family welfare schemes - objective and target group

accepted.s: Mission Parivar Vikas seeks to bring the Total Fertility Rate to 2.1 by 2025 in how many high-fertility States?
accepted.x: Mission Parivar Vikas targets a TFR of 2.1 by 2025 in seven high-fertility States.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive target-year and State-count combination.
accepted.sec: Family welfare schemes - objective and target group

accepted.s: Which of the following States is NOT included among the seven high-fertility States covered by Mission Parivar Vikas?
accepted.x: The seven States are Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Assam, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan. Odisha is not included in this list.
accepted.tq: Find the State that does not belong to the specified programme group.
accepted.sec: Family welfare schemes - objective and target group

accepted.s: Clinical outreach teams under Mission Parivar Vikas were provided for how many districts?
accepted.x: Mission Parivar Vikas included clinical outreach teams in 146 districts.
accepted.tq: Separate the programme’s district coverage figure from its State count.
accepted.sec: Family welfare schemes - objective and target group

accepted.s: Which scheme provides maternity benefits for pregnant and lactating women?
accepted.x: PM Matru Vandana Yojana 2.0 is a maternity-benefit scheme for pregnant and lactating women.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme with its specific target group.
accepted.sec: Family welfare schemes - objective and target group

accepted.s: Under the ASHA birth-spacing scheme, which of the following spacing recommendations is correct?
o: Two-year gap after marriage before the first child and three-year spacing after the first child
One-year gap after marriage and two years after the first child
Three-year gap after marriage and two-year spacing after the first child
Two-year spacing after every child, including the first
accepted.x: The scheme recommends a two-year gap after marriage before the first child and three-year spacing after the first child.
accepted.tq: Translate the scheme’s two-stage spacing rule into a practical situation.
accepted.sec: Family welfare schemes - objective and target group

accepted.s: According to the cited NFHS-6 figures, institutional deliveries increased from 88.6 per cent to:
accepted.x: Institutional deliveries increased from 88.6 per cent to 90.6 per cent.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the starting and ending values in a paired indicator.
accepted.sec: Family welfare schemes - objective and target group

accepted.s: According to the cited NFHS-6 figures, the Couple Protection Rate increased from 66.7 per cent to:
accepted.x: The Couple Protection Rate increased from 66.7 per cent to 69.1 per cent.
accepted.tq: Use precise percentage discrimination between closely placed values.
accepted.sec: Family welfare schemes - objective and target group

accepted.s: The weakest rural impact of family planning has been attributed primarily to:
o: High female literacy and late marriage
Declining son preference and improved incomes
accepted.x: The rural impact has been weakest because of social orthodoxy and psychological factors.
accepted.tq: Identify the broad causal category before selecting its examples.
accepted.sec: Barriers to family planning - rural factors, sterilisation, couple protection rate

accepted.s:
Which of the following factors are associated with weak rural acceptance of family planning?
1. Son preference
2. Viewing children as old-age insurance
3. Early marriage
4. Low female literacy
accepted.x: Son preference, dependence on children as old-age insurance, early marriage and low female literacy are all identified as barriers.
accepted.tq: Test whether all listed social and demographic barriers belong to the same group.
accepted.sec: Barriers to family planning - rural factors, sterilisation, couple protection rate

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a reason for reluctance towards sterilisation, particularly among men?
o: The increase in Couple Protection Rate
Distrust arising from the coercive sterilisation experience of 1976-77
accepted.x: Sterilisation reluctance, especially among men, is linked partly to distrust after the coercive sterilisation experience of 1976-77.
accepted.tq: Connect a present behavioural barrier with its historical cause.
accepted.sec: Barriers to family planning - rural factors, sterilisation, couple protection rate

accepted.s: Female sterilisation accounted for what percentage according to NFHS-5?
accepted.x: Female sterilisation was reported at 37.9 per cent in NFHS-5.
accepted.tq: Use exact percentage recall with evenly spaced distractors.
accepted.sec: Barriers to family planning - rural factors, sterilisation, couple protection rate

accepted.s: The Couple Protection Rate refers to the percentage of eligible couples who are:
o: Married before the legal age and protected from early marriage
Eligible for maternity benefits under PMMVY
Effectively protected against childbirth by an approved contraceptive method
accepted.x: The Couple Protection Rate is the percentage of eligible couples effectively protected against childbirth by an approved contraceptive method.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a technical demographic indicator from related welfare measures.
accepted.sec: Barriers to family planning - rural factors, sterilisation, couple protection rate

accepted.s: The National Population Policy, 2000 was declared on:
accepted.x: The National Population Policy, 2000 was declared on 15 February 2000.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact policy date from the four national dates.
accepted.sec: National Population Policy 2000 - objectives, stabilisation target years

accepted.s:
Which of the following principles formed part of the approach of the National Population Policy, 2000?
1. Target-free implementation
2. Voluntary and informed choice
3. Delivery through government, industry and NGOs
accepted.x: The policy adopted a target-free, voluntary and informed-choice approach and envisaged delivery through government, industry and NGOs.
accepted.tq: Check the policy’s approach and implementation channels together.
accepted.sec: National Population Policy 2000 - objectives, stabilisation target years

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the time horizon and objective under the National Population Policy, 2000?
o: Medium-term — Meet the unmet need for contraception
Medium-term — Bring TFR to replacement level of 2.1 by 2010
Long-term — Bring TFR to replacement level by 2010
accepted.x: The medium-term objective was to bring the TFR to the replacement level of 2.1 by 2010.
accepted.tq: Match each objective with its correct policy time horizon.
accepted.sec: National Population Policy 2000 - objectives, stabilisation target years

accepted.s: The immediate objective of the National Population Policy, 2000 was to meet the unmet need for:
accepted.x: The immediate objective was to meet the unmet need for contraception, health infrastructure and personnel.
accepted.tq: Identify the contents of the immediate objective rather than the numerical targets.
accepted.sec: National Population Policy 2000 - objectives, stabilisation target years

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the progress towards the medium-term TFR objective of the National Population Policy, 2000?
1. The target TFR was 2.1.
2. The target year was 2010.
3. The target was reached only around NFHS-5 during 2019-21.
accepted.x: The policy set a TFR target of 2.1 for 2010, but the level was reached only around NFHS-5 in 2019-21.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a policy target date from the date of its eventual achievement.
accepted.sec: National Population Policy 2000 - objectives, stabilisation target years

accepted.s: A major shortcoming attributed to the National Population Policy, 2000 is that it adopted a:
accepted.x: The policy has been criticised for its narrow, family-planning-centred view.
accepted.tq: Identify the evaluative criticism rather than a stated policy objective.
accepted.sec: National Population Policy 2000 - objectives, stabilisation target years

accepted.s: According to Census 2011, migration was recorded using which two bases?
o: Place of birth and place of last residence
accepted.x: The Census recorded migration by place of birth and by place of last residence.
accepted.tq: Recall the two official migration bases as a paired concept.
accepted.sec: Migration - Census 2011 streams, reasons, theories

accepted.s: By the place-of-last-residence criterion, how many people were migrants in India in 2011?
accepted.x: By place of last residence, 455.8 million people were migrants in 2011.
accepted.tq: Use the decimal figure and magnitude together to avoid confusing it with the decadal-movement figure.
accepted.sec: Migration - Census 2011 streams, reasons, theories

accepted.s: Of the migrants recorded by place of last residence in 2011, how many had moved during 2001-2011?
accepted.x: Out of 455.8 million migrants, 141.2 million had moved during the period 2001-2011.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the decade-specific figure from the total migrant population.
accepted.sec: Migration - Census 2011 streams, reasons, theories

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the order of inter-State female migration streams by place of last residence in 2011, from highest to lowest?
accepted.x: The order was Urban-Urban, Rural-Urban, Rural-Rural and Urban-Rural.
accepted.tq: Read the ranking carefully instead of applying the general rural-rural migration pattern.
accepted.sec: Migration - Census 2011 streams, reasons, theories

accepted.s: Which statement best explains the apparent distinction between female inter-State migration and migration across all streams in 2011?
o: Urban-Rural was the largest female stream, whereas Rural-Urban was largest across all streams.
Rural-Rural was largest in both categories because marriage was the sole reason for migration.
Urban-Urban was largest in both categories because employment was the sole reason for migration.
Urban-Urban was the largest female inter-State stream, whereas Rural-Rural was the largest across all streams and was driven largely by marriage.
accepted.x: For inter-State female migration, Urban-Urban was the largest stream; across all streams, Rural-Rural was the largest, with marriage a major driver.
accepted.tq: Separate a subgroup ranking from the ranking for the entire population.
accepted.sec: Migration - Census 2011 streams, reasons, theories

accepted.s:
Which one of the following correctly matches the main migration reason with the group mentioned?

1. Women — Marriage
2. Men — Work
3. Gulf migration — International migration context
accepted.x: Marriage is the major stated reason for women’s migration, work for men’s migration, and Gulf migration represents the international migration context.
accepted.tq: Match reasons and examples with the appropriate migration category.
accepted.sec: Migration - Census 2011 streams, reasons, theories

accepted.s: Who propounded the Laws of Migration in 1885?
accepted.x: E.G. Ravenstein propounded the Laws of Migration in 1885.
accepted.tq: Use the year-theorist association as the decisive clue.
accepted.sec: Migration - Census 2011 streams, reasons, theories

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Push-pull theory and intervening obstacles — Everett Lee
2. Expected-income rural-urban model — Michael Todaro
3. Laws of Migration — E.G. Ravenstein
accepted.x: Everett Lee is associated with push-pull theory and intervening obstacles, Michael Todaro with the expected-income rural-urban model, and E.G. Ravenstein with the Laws of Migration.
accepted.tq: Start from the familiar theorist pair and verify all three associations.
accepted.sec: Migration - Census 2011 streams, reasons, theories

accepted.s: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment froze Lok Sabha and State Assembly seats on the basis of the 1971 Census until:
accepted.x: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 froze the allocation of seats based on the 1971 Census until 2000.
accepted.tq: Separate the original freeze period from its later extension.
accepted.sec: Population stabilisation incentives - two-child norms, seat freeze amendments

accepted.s: Which amendment extended the freeze on seat allocation until the first Census after 2026?
accepted.x: The 84th Amendment of 2001 extended the freeze until the first Census after 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the amendment that created the freeze from the amendment that extended it.
accepted.sec: Population stabilisation incentives - two-child norms, seat freeze amendments

accepted.s: The fear that southern States may lose approximately how many Lok Sabha seats is associated with future delimitation?
accepted.x: The delimitation concern is that southern States could lose approximately 8-10 Lok Sabha seats.
accepted.tq: Use the range-based numerical clue rather than a single figure.
accepted.sec: Population stabilisation incentives - two-child norms, seat freeze amendments

accepted.s: Seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies are allotted on the basis of population under which Articles?
accepted.x: Articles 82 and 170 relate to the allocation and readjustment of seats on the basis of population.
accepted.tq: Use Article-number discrimination between parliamentary and local-government provisions.
accepted.sec: Population stabilisation incentives - two-child norms, seat freeze amendments

accepted.s: Which change is associated with Andhra Pradesh’s draft population policy of March 2026?
o: Introduction of a three-child norm for local elections
Removal of the two-child norm for local body elections
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh draft policy proposed removing the two-child norm for local body elections.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy change by spotting the reversal of the existing norm.
accepted.sec: Population stabilisation incentives - two-child norms, seat freeze amendments

accepted.s: The National Commission on Population was set up in 2000 under the chairmanship of the:
accepted.x: The National Commission on Population was established in 2000 under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister.
accepted.tq: Apply the who-chairs-the-body pattern in institutional questions.
accepted.sec: Population bodies and reports

accepted.s:
The National Commission on Population includes which of the following categories of members?
1. Chief Ministers
2. Union Ministers
3. Representatives only from local bodies
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Commission includes Chief Ministers and Union Ministers. It is not composed only of representatives from local bodies.
accepted.tq: Reject the restrictive composition statement and retain the two stated categories.
accepted.sec: Population bodies and reports

accepted.s: The State of World Population report is published by:
accepted.x: The State of World Population report is published by the United Nations Population Fund, or UNFPA.
accepted.tq: Distinguish among closely related United Nations agencies by their reports.
accepted.sec: Population bodies and reports

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the institutional arrangement for the National Family Health Survey?
o: It is conducted by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare through IIPS, Mumbai.
It is conducted by UNFPA through the National Commission on Population.
It is conducted by the Ministry of Finance through the World Bank.
It is conducted by NITI Aayog through State Election Commissions.
accepted.x: The NFHS is associated with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and is conducted through the International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai.
accepted.tq: Use the ministry-agency association and reject neighbouring institutional bodies.
accepted.sec: Population bodies and reports

accepted.s: NFHS-6 covered approximately how many households in how many districts?
accepted.x: NFHS-6 covered 6.79 lakh households across 715 districts.
accepted.tq: Keep the household figure and district figure paired accurately.
accepted.sec: Population bodies and reports
